subject: GlassStream: RFP Assurance Workbook — control mapping & evidence intake plan
messages:
From: Anna Liu <anna.liu@glassstream.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: vendor-relations@glassstream.com
Date: Thu, 7 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: GlassStream RFP: assurance workbook and control mapping request

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is GlassStream's assurance workbook (full RFP package attached as tab 'Workbook'). Procurement has asked that vendors map each questionnaire/control to the provider's attestation or artifact (SOC 2, ISO 27001 clause, or compensating control evidence). Key asks from legal/procurement:

- A control-to-evidence crosswalk for the SOC 2/ISO items called out in tab 'Controls'
- A secure delivery mechanism for any sensitive artifacts (SOC 2 report, key control runbooks, KMS proof)
- A timeline for when GlassStream will receive the first evidence bundle (we need something by Jan 21 for procurement review)

Please confirm scope: do you plan to provide full, unredacted SOC 2 report or a redacted version plus control mappings? Also, we need to understand your KMS provenance proof (do you provide HSM/KMS audit records or a statement + runbook).

Attached: GlassStream_RFP_Assurance_Workbook.xlsx

Can you confirm the internal point-of-contact and proposed delivery cadence?

Best,
Anna Liu
CISO, GlassStream
anna.liu@glassstream.com
--
GlassStream Inc.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Anna Liu <anna.liu@glassstream.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 7 Jan 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: GlassStream RFP: assurance workbook and control mapping request

Anna — thanks, received the workbook. Looping in Neha (Assurance) and Priyom (Controls) to scope artifact packaging and delivery. High level plan below; we'll follow up with a slot for a kickoff call tomorrow.

Proposed approach:
1) Quick triage (today): identify which GlassStream controls map directly to our SOC 2 Type II report and to ISO 27001 controls. Deliverable: control_map_snapshot.pdf (initial mapping).
2) Evidence sprint (Jan 11–14): collect primary artifacts (runbooks, configuration screenshots, KMS proof summary, retention policy, backup test logs). We'll package in staged bundles to avoid sending an unredacted SOC 2 report in the first tranche.
3) Delivery (Jan 14): initial evidence packet + redacted attestation summary; follow-on delivery (Jan 18–20) if procurement needs unredacted report under NDA.

Questions for GlassStream (please confirm):
- Is redacted SOC 2 acceptable for initial procurement review, with unredacted available under NDA?
- Any specific controls you want prioritized (e.g., crypto/key management, separation of duties, privileged access)?

Neha/Priyom — can you confirm owners and whether we should use the secured SFTP or the new evidence portal (link below) for GlassStream?

Attachments: Redwood_ControlInventory_v2.xlsx
Related link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-GlassStream-Intake

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: GlassStream RFP — artifact intake plan

Karthik / Priyom —

Following up on Karthik's note. I did a quick pass on the workbook and flagged ~38 controls that will require primary artifacts (not just statements). Priority areas: KMS/key provenance, backup/restoration tests, privileged access reviews, and change control evidence.

Here is what I recommend we collect in the first packet (Jan 14):
- Redacted SOC 2 Type II (only table-of-contents + testing summary redacted; control evidence pages intact where possible)
- KMS proof: key rotation schedule, KMS audit log extracts (last 90 days), and a short note on HSM provider
- Backup evidence: snapshot of backup job history + restore test runbook + one restore test result
- PAM/privileged access: list of privileged roles + recent access review artifacts (redacted usernames ok)
- Network segmentation: VPC diagram + security group baseline screenshot

I created an artifact manifest template and will push to the shared intake folder. Priyom, can you lead collection and redaction, and confirm whether we need any legal-approved cover letter for the SOC 2 extract?

Attachment: artifact_manifest_template.csv

Neha
Senior Assurance Manager
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Subject: Re: GlassStream RFP: assurance workbook and control mapping request — initial evidence packet delivered

Anna — attaching the first delivery for GlassStream procurement. This tranche includes the items we agreed to in the intake plan.

What we're delivering now (Jan 14):
- control_map_snapshot.pdf — initial control mapping (SOC 2 / ISO clause pointers for each workbook control)
- RSW-GlassStream_Evidence_Packet_01.zip (stub) — stubbed archive listing: redacted_SOC2_summary.pdf, kms_audit_extract_90days.csv (redacted), backup_test_result_20261220.pdf, pam_access_review_redacted.pdf, vpc_baseline_sg.png
- control_map_snapshot.pdf (attached again for quick reference)

Notes and next steps:
- Redacted SOC 2 summary included. We can provide the unredacted report under an NDA — please confirm procurement's NDA template or we can share ours.
- KMS audit extracts are redacted to remove customer-specific IDs; if GlassStream needs raw audit records for their legal review we can route via our secure SFTP under an approved DPA/NDA.
- Remaining artifacts (deeper telemetry logs and config exports) will be prepared for Jan 18 delivery. If you want the unredacted SOC 2 earlier, let us know and we'll accelerate legal review.

Attachments: RSW-GlassStream_Evidence_Packet_01.zip (stub), control_map_snapshot.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if procurement wants a walkthrough of the packet.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Controls Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com
